variants.title: G4NA - Specifications and Variants
variants.intro: The G4NA is a specific engine code within Hyundai Motor Group's Nu family, which also includes G4NB (1.8L), G4NC, G4ND, G4NE and others. Unlike some Hyundai/Kia engines with multiple distinct sub-codes, the G4NA primarily varies by tune and application rather than fundamental hardware differences. Key technical specifications: - Displacement: 1,999 cc - Bore × Stroke: 81.0 mm × 97.0 mm - Compression ratio: 10.3:1 - Cylinder block: Aluminium with thin-walled cast-iron liners - Cylinder head: Aluminium, 16-valve DOHC - Valvetrain: Hydraulic lifters (no manual adjustment required) - Timing drive: Chain - Phase regulation: Yes (variable valve timing on both camshafts) - Fuel system: Multi-point (distributed) injection (MPI) - Intake: Plastic manifold with VIS (Variable Intake System) geometry change - Turbocharging: No (naturally aspirated) - Oil capacity: 4.5 litres (some variants 6.5 litres with larger sump) - Recommended oil: 5W-20 or 5W-30 - Weight: Approximately 117 kg - Euro standard: Euro 4 / Euro 5 Power output variations by application: - 150-152 hp: Lower-tune applications (certain Hyundai i40, Kia Soul variants) - 156-161 hp: Mid-range tune (Elantra, Cerato, some Tucson/Sportage) - 162-167 hp: Higher-tune applications (Sonata, Optima, K5) Key revision (2017): Oil piston cooling nozzles were added to reduce cylinder scoring risk. This is a significant durability improvement - post-2017 G4NA units are generally preferred for replacement purchases.

relatives.description: The Theta II 2.0-litre petrol engine that the G4NA replaced in most applications. The G4KD suffered timing chain and oil consumption issues that the Nu-series addressed with revised piston rings and oil passages.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement G4NA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used G4NA can make sense for low-value host vehicles (older i40, ix35, Soul) where a £2,000+ reconditioned unit would exceed the vehicle's worth. However, the used market carries significant risk - the cylinder scoring issue is often already present but not yet symptomatic. Only consider a used G4NA if: (1) it comes from a post-2017 vehicle with the revised oil piston cooling nozzles, (2) the seller can provide a compression test and endoscopy report, and (3) the catalytic converter is confirmed healthy.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A properly reconditioned G4NA is the strongest option for most owners. A quality recon should include: cylinder re-honing with new piston rings (addressing the scoring risk), new timing chain and tensioner, new valve stem seals, new gaskets and seals throughout, and a thorough inspection of the cylinder head. Crucially, the catalytic converter must be replaced or verified as healthy - otherwise the new engine will suffer the same fate. Reconditioned units typically carry a 12-24 month warranty, giving peace of mind that a used engine cannot offer.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified when the vehicle itself has strong retained value (e.g. a well-maintained Santa Fe or Optima) and the owner wants to retain the original engine. For the G4NA, an upgraded rebuild should include: new pistons and rings (upgraded design where available), new timing chain and tensioner, new catalytic converter, and the addition of oil piston cooling nozzles if retrofitting to a pre-2017 block. A rebuild is more expensive than a reconditioned exchange unit but may be the right choice for low-mileage, high-specification vehicles.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All options can be supplied and fitted through our network of UK Hyundai/Kia specialists - we handle the logistics, warranty coordination and nationwide delivery so you get a turnkey solution.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The G4NA is found across a wide value spectrum - from £2,000-£4,000 older Hyundai i40 and Kia Soul examples, through £5,000-£12,000 Tucson and Sportage models, up to £8,000-£18,000 Santa Fe and Optima examples. **For vehicles valued under £4,000, a reconditioned G4NA at £2,000+ supply-only represents 50%+ of the vehicle's value - evaluate scrap/part-ex value carefully before committing.** For higher-value examples (£6,000+), the replacement cost is typically well within the vehicle's worth and represents a sound investment in continued reliable motoring.

mainEntity.name: How much does a G4NA engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned G4NA supply-only unit typically costs £2,000-£3,200, with used units from £500-£1,200. Fitted prices add 7-9 hours of labour at independent specialist rates. Used G4NA engines: £500-£1,200 supply-only. Reconditioned G4NA: £2,000-£3,200 supply-only. Rebuilt G4NA: £2,800-£4,000 supply-only. Labour: 7-9 hours at approximately £65-£85 per hour.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the G4NA engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most frequently reported G4NA issues are: cylinder bore scoring caused by catalytic converter debris ingestion, leading to oil consumption and loss of compression; progressive oil consumption in high-mileage units; and timing chain tensioner wear causing rattle on cold start. Catalyst disintegration releases ceramic particles that score cylinder walls. Oil consumption can reach 1L per 1,000 km in affected units. Timing chain tensioner wear is a known issue from 80,000 miles onward.

mainEntity.name: Which Hyundai and Kia models use the G4NA engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G4NA was fitted across a wide range of Hyundai and Kia models from 2010 to 2018, primarily in 2.0-litre petrol variants. Hyundai models include i40 (VF), Tucson (TL), ix35 (LM facelift), Santa Fe (DM), Elantra (MD/AD), Sonata (LF), and Creta. Kia models include Optima (TF/JF), Sportage (SL/QL), Soul (AM/PS), Cerato (YD/BD), Carens (RP), and K5 (DL3).

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned G4NA?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used G4NA only makes sense for low-value vehicles (under £4,000) where a reconditioned unit would be uneconomical. However, used engines carry significant risk of undetected cylinder scoring or catalytic converter damage. A reconditioned unit is strongly recommended - a proper recon includes cylinder re-honing, new piston rings, new timing chain and tensioner, and most importantly, a new or verified catalyst to prevent the same failure recurring. Reconditioned units come with a 12-24 month warranty.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the G4NA engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G4NA engine code is stamped on a flat metal pad on the cylinder block - typically visible near the front of the engine, above the exhaust manifold or behind the alternator. It also appears on the V5C registration document under 'Engine number' (the first characters will be G4NA). If unsure, enter your registration above and we'll confirm the exact fitment.

mainEntity.name: What is the lifespan of a G4NA engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance - regular oil changes (5W-20 or 5W-30 every 5,000-7,000 miles) and early replacement of a failing catalytic converter - the G4NA can reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work is required. Post-2017 units with oil piston cooling nozzles are more durable and may exceed 200,000 miles. However, ignoring oil consumption or catalyst degradation can shorten life to 80,000-100,000 miles.
